importantFindings.title: The stamp comparison misses any server row older than the device's newest stamp, so stale cards do not always fail safe (DI-B7-Q2 stays partly open)
importantFindings.evidence: keep_course refuses only when a row's updatedAt is greater than the single value in give_up (supabase/migrations/20261104000000_keep_course.sql, `latest.changed collate "C" > coalesce(give_up ->> latest.course, '')`). updatedAt is the time of the edit on the phone, not the time of upload (src/persistence/stamp.ts), so a phone's offline work arrives with old stamps. Run on real Postgres. Case A: the server holds a row at T1 that the device saw, plus two rows stamped T0 that it never saw; give_up {X: T1} returned 'kept' and all three rows were erased. Case B: a device clock ahead sent give_up {X: 2030}; a server row at T1 it never saw was erased too. This contradicts 03_TECHNICAL_DECISIONS.md ('so a choice is never made on what the owner did not see') and the SQL header ('only if what it holds is what the owner saw'). Why I do not rate it a blocker: a whole unseen course is now refused, the kept course is untouched, and the rows lost belong to a course the owner explicitly gave up after an irreversible warning. The window is also narrow: the device must confirm before its download catches up after reconnecting. That is my reading of the 04 B7 predicate, and the orchestrator may read it differently. Either change the rule, for example a per-course digest of (id, updatedAt) or at least row counts in give_up, or correct both texts and record the limit for the owner.
importantFindings.reproduction: Throwaway script in my scratchpad's b7di/r2/ (pgr2.mjs, same migrations and harness as .evidence/B7/keep-rule-local-postgres.mjs). Observed: 'A keep with give_up X=T1, server holds 2 rows the device never saw, stamped T0: kept {"courses":["K"],"students":[]}' and 'B give_up X=2030 (device clock ahead), server row at T1 unseen: kept {"courses":["K"],"students":[]}'. Expected from the contract's wording: CVNEW.
importantFindings.specRef: 03_TECHNICAL_DECISIONS.md, 'Several courses on one account (B7)'; 04_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md B7, checklist 'the two courses reached offline'

qolFindings.title: keep_course can lose a deadlock against an edit of a course row
qolFindings.evidence: In 150 rounds of keep_course racing two course-row updates on real Postgres, keep_course ended with 40P01 in 5 rounds and nothing was erased in those rounds. In 1 further round keep_course succeeded and both edits got 40P01. No round left a wrong state. The likely cause, inferred from the tally and not traced, is opposite lock order: keep_course takes the advisory lock then the row, while an update holds the row when its trigger asks for the advisory lock. Uploads already retry 40P01 (src/backup/uploadPolicy.ts). keepCourse would show this as no-answer or refused, depending on the status PostgREST sends (not checked), and Riprova is safe either way.
qolFindings.reproduction: pgr2.mjs case C in my scratchpad's b7di/r2/. Tally: kept with both edits ok 144; kept with both edits 40P01 1; keep 40P01 with both edits ok 3; keep 40P01 with one edit also 40P01 2.

qolFindings.title: A malformed refusal is dropped silently once any held course leaves
qolFindings.evidence: storedCourseId returns undefined on bad JSON, and with no standing course dropRefusalsOfGoneCourses deletes the row (src/persistence/migrations.ts). Observed: the open succeeded and the refusals list came back empty. This is the right trade against a locked device, and only a corrupt row reaches it. Recorded so the behaviour is known.
qolFindings.reproduction: Throwaway r2d.spec.ts in my scratchpad's b7di/: plant data '{not json', remove a course, reload. Observed: 'AFTER LEAVE error false | refusals []'.
qolFindings.specRef: 03_TECHNICAL_DECISIONS.md: 'This housekeeping can never fail an open'
